title: Calcium measurements in enzymatically dissociated or mechanically microdissected mouse primary skeletal muscle fibers
protocol: Sacrifice the animal according to locally approved procedures.
Amputate the leg at the level of the ankle joint using sharp surgical scissors.
Place the foot in prewarmed Tyrode solution.
Pin the outermost toes of the isolated foot with dissection needles on the dissection pad with the plantar side up.
Remove the skin overlaying the FDB muscle using dissection scissors.
Grip and lift the proximal tendon of the FDB muscle using forceps.
Make a transverse incision to separate the FDB tendon from its origin at the back of the heel (calcaneus).
Carefully cut and remove all soft and connective tissue between the FDB muscle and the flexor digitorum longus (FDL) using forceps and dissection scissors.
Point the dissection scissors towards the FDL to minimize fiber damage.
Cut the FDB tendons as far out on the toes as possible to leave a long distal tendon.
Fold back the freed portion of the FDB onto the part of the FDB that remains joined by connective tissue to the underlying FDL muscle.
Do not stretch the FDB muscle during dissection.
Place 50 mL of complete DMEM/F12 in an incubator at 37°C.
Prepare 5 mL of supplemented collagenase type 1.
Clean FDB muscles of tendons, connective tissue, and blood vessels.
Incubate the cleaned muscle for 2–3 h at 37°C in the supplemented type 1 collagenase.
Transfer muscles to 3 mL fresh DMEM/F12 that was prewarmed in step 10.
Gently triturate the muscle using a regular blue plastic 1 mL pipette tip filled with 900 μL DMEM/F12.
Pipette slowly 10–20 times up and down to separate individual muscle fibers.
Transfer a volume of 300 μL of the resultant muscle fiber suspension in laminin-coated 35 mm glass-bottom Petri dishes.
Allow fibers to attach for 15 min at 37°C.
Add a further 2.7 mL of supplemented DMEM/F12.
Place the FDB muscle in a custom-made dissection tray equipped with a pair of hollow movable metal 10G syringe needles mounted at opposite ends.
Fix both tendons of the muscle by inserting them into the split ends of a nylon rod located inside the syringe needles.
Remove connective tissue, fat, and visible blood vessels using sharpened dissection forceps and scissors to make FDB fibers accessible.
Separate the FDB muscle longitudinally into three FDB digits.
Keep some muscle fibers of each FDB digit attached to the tendons at both sides (proximal and distal) for isolation.
Mount one digit in the dissection tray.
Fix the mounted digit into the split rods on both sides.
Apply single electrical stimuli using a pen stimulator at supramaximal voltage (≤10 V).
Select twitching fibers positioned on the FDB surface under 40× magnification.
Isolate selected fibers by cutting and removing all other fibers in small steps.
Check remaining fibers repeatedly to identify those that give robust contraction upon electrical stimulation.
Carefully remove other fibers using jeweller’s forceps and micro-iris scissors, ensuring not to damage isolated fiber.
Verify the isolated single fiber contracts upon electrical stimulation.
Trim the proximal and distal tendons of mechanically dissected single fibers longitudinally.
Fit the trimmed tendons into aluminum or platinum T-clips using two pairs of forceps to fold the T-clips.
Clamp the T-clips as close as possible to the muscle fiber.
Install a micropipette in a micromanipulator.
Load the micropipette with approximately 0.5 μL of 10 mM indo-1 salt solution.
Mount the fiber in the recording chamber between a force transducer and an adjustable holder.
Mount the stimulation chamber onto an inverted microscope.
Supperfuse the fiber with Tyrode solution at 31°C.
Determine the supramaximal stimulation intensity by stimulating with 70 Hz tetani and increasing voltage until the stimulation is 10%–20% above maximum force.
Adjust the fiber length to obtain maximum tetanic force using the movable screw.
Position the tip of the injection micropipette near the fiber.
Measure background fluorescence of the fiber at 405 and 495 nm.
Subtract background fluorescence from the recorded signal values.
Inject the fiber with the dye.
Incubate the fiber in the diluted indo-1 AM dye for at least 1 h at room temperature (20°C–25°C) to allow the dye to diffuse into the fiber.
Ensure the fiber does not dry out during loading by placing a water-filled cap from an Eppendorf tube in the incubation dish and sealing it tightly with Parafilm.
Supernatant the fiber with Tyrode solution for approximately 30 min to remove any remaining dye outside of the fiber before starting the measurement.
Load the fiber with calcium indicator dye using injection or loading method.
Measure fluorescence in the dark with excitation at 360 nm and dual emission at 405 nm and 495 nm.
Close the shutter for the excitation light when measurements are not performed.
Stimulate the fiber with supramaximal electrical pulses (0.5 ms in duration).
Stimulate the fiber for 350 ms at frequencies between 15–150 Hz every minute.
